verdict.rationale: OpenClaw's scheduler documents outbound delivery of automation job output to a webhook ([openclaw-docs-27], [openclaw-docs-59]), which is a real outbound HTTP callback that a programmatic consumer can receive. That coverage is limited to scheduled-job results rather than general event subscriptions. The Gateway HTTP hooks ([openclaw-docs-28]) are inbound triggers that wake an agent, so they don't count toward subscribing to events. Missing for 10: a general event catalog with subscribable outbound webhooks (e.g. message, session, tool or agent-run events), documented registration/management of webhook endpoints, payload schema, signing/retry semantics, and independent corroboration.
